gloss: to look/act mature, to seem grown-up

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {大人|おとな}びませんでした

forms.negative: {大人|おとな}びていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {大人|おとな}びていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to look or act mature, to seem grown-up
definitions.explanation: Describes a young person whose appearance, behavior, or manner seems older or more mature than their actual age. Can apply to physical appearance, speech, or demeanor.

examples.japanese: {大人|おとな}びた{表情|ひょうじょう}をしている。
examples.english: She has a mature expression on her face.

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}は{同|おな}じ{年|とし}の{子|こ}より{大人|おとな}びて{見|み}える。
examples.english: That child looks more mature than kids the same age.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}った{姪|めい}は、すっかり{大人|おとな}びた{話|はな}し{方|かた}をするようになっていた。
examples.english: My niece, whom I hadn't seen in a while, had come to speak in a very grown-up way.

notes:
{大人|おとな}びる is an intransitive verb most commonly used in the past participle form {大人|おとな}びた as a modifier.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive)
- Pattern: [person]が{大人|おとな}びる

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {大人|おとな}びた{顔|かお}: a mature-looking face
- {大人|おとな}びた{話|はな}し{方|かた}: a grown-up way of speaking
- {大人|おとな}びた{雰囲気|ふんいき}: a mature atmosphere/aura
- {大人|おとな}びて{見|み}える: to look mature

The word carries a generally positive or neutral connotation, suggesting poise or composure beyond one's years. It is primarily used about children or teenagers, not about adults.
